source: Karnataka NMMS MAT 2022-23 question paper, NMMS-MAT (K-8) P-1 (pyq/ka-2022-23-mat.pdf). The paper has no answer key, so every answer here is worked out by us.

sections.directions: Complete the following number series by choosing the correct number from the given choices.
The wrong number in the given series is:
Complete the given analogy by selecting the correct answer from the given choices.
The odd one out of the following is:

Choose the numbers/signs which should be interchanged to get the correct equation among given alternatives.
Find the missing number in the given matrices.
Find the missing letter in the given matrices.
The following questions are based on the numbers and letters arranged in the pyramid pattern. Study the pattern and complete the given analogy.
Read the following information and answer the questions below it.
In the following questions, a word is written according to some code. In the same way find the code for the other given word.
The following Venn diagrams show the relationship among the three given persons/objects. Identify the appropriate diagram to show the relationship among them.

Assume the given statements are true and decide which of the following conclusions follow logically from these statements.

questions.prompt: Find the missing number in the matrix.
questions.rule: In each row, (1st number)³ + (3rd number)² = the middle number.

questions.rule: In each column, multiply the top three numbers and halve the result to get the bottom number.

questions.prompt: Find the missing letter in the matrix.
questions.rule: Use letter places. In each row, (1st − 2nd)² is the place of the 3rd letter.

questions.prompt: Find the missing letter in the matrix.
questions.rule: Rows 1 and 3 go forward 5 and then 3 letters; row 2 goes back 5 and then 3.

questions.prompt: Find the missing letter in the matrix.

questions.working: E, K, Q (+6 each time); Q, S, U (+2 each time)

questions.prompt: How many rectangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Count the single boxes first, then the rectangles made of two or more boxes next to each other.
questions.working: Counting every rectangle, from the smallest boxes up to the whole figure, gives 18.

questions.prompt: How many triangles and how many squares are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Count the triangles and the squares separately. Only shapes with all four sides equal and square corners count as squares.
questions.working: Counting every shape carefully gives 10 triangles and 6 squares.

questions.prompt: Which figure has 16 triangles?
questions.rule: Count the triangles in each figure: every triangle is made of three lines that meet in pairs.
questions.working: A has 16, B has 18, C has 20 and D has 10.

questions.prompt: A + B means A is the daughter of B; A × B means A is the son of B; A − B means A is the wife of B. If P × Q − S, which statement is correct?

options.A: S is the wife of Q
options.B: S is the father of P
options.C: P is the daughter of Q
options.D: Q is the father of P

questions.rule: P × Q: P is the son of Q. Q − S: Q is the wife of S.
questions.working: So S is Q's husband, and P's father.

questions.prompt: A + B means A is the daughter of B; A × B means A is the son of B; A − B means A is the wife of B. If T − S × B − M, which statement is wrong?

options.A: B is the mother of S
options.B: M is the husband of B
options.C: T is the wife of S
options.D: S is the daughter of B

questions.rule: T − S: T is the wife of S. S × B: S is the son of B. B − M: B is the wife of M.
questions.working: S is B's son, not daughter, so D is wrong; the others are true.

questions.prompt: Q is the father of P. R and S are sisters. The son of P is the brother of S. How is Q related to R?
questions.rule: P's son is S's brother, so S (and her sister R) are P's children too.
questions.working: Q is P's father, so Q is R's grandfather.

questions.prompt: TEMPLE is coded as VHQNIA. How is CHURCH coded?
questions.rule: The letters move +2, +3, +4, then −2, −3, −4: T → V, E → H, M → Q, P → N, L → I, E → A.
questions.working: C + 2 = E, H + 3 = K, U + 4 = Y, R − 2 = P, C − 3 = Z, H − 4 = D, so EKYPZD

questions.prompt: COMPUTER is coded as RFUVQNPC. How is STUDENTS coded?
questions.rule: Write the word backwards (RETUPMOC), keep the first and last letters, and move each letter in between one place forward.
questions.working: STUDENTS backwards is STNEDUTS; S, then T N E D U T each +1 = U O F E V U, then S: SUOFEVUS

questions.prompt: DRIVER = 12, SMILE = 10, ACCIDENT = 16. What is the code for CAR?
questions.rule: The code is twice the number of letters: DRIVER has 6 letters, 6 × 2 = 12.
questions.working: CAR has 3 letters: 3 × 2 = 6

questions.prompt: This net is folded into a cube. How many dots are on the face opposite the face with six dots?
questions.rule: In a straight line of squares, the 1st and 3rd are opposite. Two squares stuck on opposite sides of the line, one on the left and one on the right, are also opposite.
questions.working: The column reads 4, 3, 2, 1: 4 is opposite 2 and 3 is opposite 1. The 5 sticks out on the left and the 6 on the right, so 6 is opposite 5.

questions.prompt: This sheet is folded into a cube. Which arrangement of signs is on the face opposite face 3?
questions.rule: Faces 1, 2, 4 and 5 fold up round face 3, and the four triangles fold over the top to make the face opposite 3.
questions.working: Looking down on that face, each triangle stays on its own side: + at the top, − on the left, = on the right and × at the bottom: B.

questions.prompt: The six faces of a cube are marked a, b, c, d, e and f. Three positions of the cube are shown. Which net does the cube unfold into?
questions.rule: Find the opposite pairs from the views: a face can't be opposite any face seen next to it.
questions.working: b is seen with f, d, a and c, so b is opposite e. f is seen with b, d, c and e, so f is opposite a. That leaves d opposite c. Only net C has f–a, d–c and b–e opposite.

questions.prompt: If 1 January 2022 is a Saturday, on which day is Republic Day celebrated in the same year?
questions.rule: Republic Day is 26 January, 25 days after 1 January. Divide by 7 and keep the remainder.
questions.working: 25 = 3 × 7 + 4, so 4 days after Saturday: Wednesday

questions.prompt: If 15 August 2021 was a Friday, what day of the week will 15 August 2025 be?
questions.rule: Count the odd days: each ordinary year adds 1 and a leap year adds 2. From 15 August 2021 to 15 August 2025 there are 4 years, and 29 February 2024 comes in between.
questions.working: 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 5 odd days, so 5 days after Friday: Wednesday
questions.note: 15 August 2021 was really a Sunday; the question asks you to take it as a Friday.

questions.prompt: Divya walks north from her home. Then she turns right and walks, again turns right and walks, and finally turns left and walks. Which direction is she going now?
questions.rule: Turning right goes one quarter clockwise round North → East → South → West; turning left goes back one.
questions.working: North → right → East → right → South → left → East

questions.prompt: Mohan walks 5 km north from his home, then turns right and walks 8 km, and again turns right and walks 11 km. How far is he from his home now?
questions.rule: Draw the walk. The straight-line distance home is found with Pythagoras.
questions.working: He ends 11 − 5 = 6 km south and 8 km east of home: √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Authors, Teachers, Farmers?
questions.rule: A person can be any two of these, or all three, so all three circles overlap each other.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Mothers, Ladies, Doctors?
questions.rule: All mothers are ladies, so that circle is inside. Some doctors are ladies and some are mothers, so the doctors circle cuts both.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Squares, Quadrilaterals, Polygons?
questions.rule: Every square is a quadrilateral and every quadrilateral is a polygon, so the circles sit one inside another.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows the relation between: Boys, Men, Girls?
questions.rule: If boys are counted as males, they sit inside a "men" circle and girls are separate.
questions.note: Boys, men and girls are three separate groups (three circles apart), which is not among the options. Diagram e (boys inside men, girls apart) is the closest; check the official key.

questions.prompt: A, B, C, D and E are sitting around a circle facing the centre. B is between C and D. D is second to the right of A. E is not between A and C. Which statement is true?

options.A: 'E' is to the immediate left of 'B'
options.C: 'D' is to the immediate left of 'E'

questions.rule: Facing the centre, your right is the anticlockwise way round. Place A, then D two places to its right; B must sit between C and D, and E takes the last place, between D and A.
questions.working: Clockwise round the circle: A, C, B, D, E. So C sits between A and B.

questions.prompt: A, B, C, D and E are sitting around a circle facing the centre. B is between C and D. D is second to the right of A. E is not between A and C. What is the position of 'A'?
questions.rule: Facing the centre, your right is the anticlockwise way round. Place A, then D two places to its right; B must sit between C and D, and E takes the last place, between D and A.
questions.working: Clockwise round the circle: A, C, B, D, E. Going right (anticlockwise) from B: C, then A. So A is second to the right of B.

questions.prompt: A, B, C, D and E are sitting around a circle facing the centre. B is between C and D. D is second to the right of A. E is not between A and C. 'E' is sitting between which two?
questions.rule: Facing the centre, your right is the anticlockwise way round. Place A, then D two places to its right; B must sit between C and D, and E takes the last place, between D and A.
questions.working: Clockwise round the circle: A, C, B, D, E. E sits between D and A.

questions.prompt: Rohith completes a piece of work in 6 days and Rahul completes the same work in 12 days. In how many days will they complete it together?
questions.rule: Add the parts of the work each one does in a day.
questions.working: Rohith does 1/6 and Rahul 1/12 a day: 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4, so together they take 4 days

questions.prompt: If a fixed amount doubles in 12 years at simple interest, what is the rate of interest?
questions.rule: If an amount doubles, the interest equals the amount: 100% in 12 years.

questions.prompt: The speeds of four trains are given below. Which is the highest speed?
questions.rule: Change every speed to km/hr: × 3.6 for m/second, × 60 ÷ 1000 for m/minute.
questions.working: 25 m/s = 90 km/hr; 1800 m/min = 108 km/hr; 72 km/hr; 36000 m/hr = 36 km/hr. The fastest is 1800 m/minute.

questions.prompt: What is the angle between the minute hand and the hour hand of a clock at 6:50 in the morning?
questions.rule: The minute hand moves 6° a minute; the hour hand moves 30° an hour plus 0.5° a minute.

questions.prompt: A clock shows 4 o'clock. Through how many degrees does the hour hand turn in the next 10 minutes?
questions.rule: The hour hand turns 30° in 60 minutes, so 0.5° every minute.

questions.prompt: How many times do the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock come together in a day?
questions.rule: The hands come together 11 times in every 12 hours (once between 11 and 1, at 12 o'clock).
questions.working: 11 × 2 = 22 times in a day

questions.prompt: In the series below, how many even numbers have an odd number on both sides?

questions.prompt: In the series below, how many 2's come immediately after a prime number?

questions.prompt: In the series below, how many pairs of numbers next to each other differ by 3?
questions.rule: Go through the series one place at a time and mark every place that fits, then count the marks.

questions.prompt: In the series below, what is the 3rd number to the right of the 8th number from the left?
questions.rule: Count from the left to the 8th number, then 3 more to the right.

questions.rule: Find the part inside the circle and outside the rectangle and triangle.

questions.prompt:
Statements:
(1) All crows are pigeons.
(2) All pigeons are parrots.
Conclusions:
(I) All pigeons are crows.
(II) All crows are parrots.
Take the statements as true. Which conclusions follow?

options.C: Both I and II are correct
options.D: Both I and II are wrong

questions.rule: Draw the groups as circles in every way the statements allow. A conclusion follows only if it is true in every drawing.
questions.working: Crows are inside pigeons, and pigeons inside parrots, so all crows are parrots (II). Some pigeons need not be crows, so I does not follow.

questions.prompt:
Statements:
(1) All papers are books.
(2) Some books are pens.
Conclusions:
(I) Some books are papers.
(II) Some pens are books.
Take the statements as true. Which conclusions follow?

options.C: Both I and II are correct
options.D: Both I and II are wrong

questions.rule: Draw the groups as circles in every way the statements allow. A conclusion follows only if it is true in every drawing.
questions.working: All papers are books, so some books are papers (I). Some books are pens, so some pens are books (II).
